- When sentiment is negative and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (prices trending down then reversing), model should not over-forecast upward momentum.  
- Overshoots after spikes (especially in early forecast days) are common — cap forecasted values at 1.5x the 14-day moving average.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative, model should underweight short-term volatility and favor downward bias in 30-day forecasts.  
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum after a dip, model should not lag — adjust forecast to match the sentiment’s direction by day 3–5.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong upward movement, model should not overcorrect downward — maintain momentum unless sentiment turns negative.
